prompt: Compare the official or actively maintained Python clients for Redis Streams and RabbitMQ. Find documentation for synchronous and async workers, and identify which projects maintain each client.
Compare Redis Streams and RabbitMQ delivery guarantees for Python workers. Use official documentation and distinguish acknowledgements, redelivery, and duplicate processing.
Compare persistence and crash recovery for Redis Streams and RabbitMQ quorum queues. Identify documented configuration requirements and cases where acknowledged data can be lost.
Compare message ordering in Redis Streams consumer groups and RabbitMQ queues. Focus on multiple workers, redelivery, and what applications must do to preserve per-key order.
Compare retry and dead-letter handling for Redis Streams and RabbitMQ. Identify built-in mechanisms and which parts a Python worker must implement. Use official documentation.
Compare how Redis Streams and RabbitMQ handle slow consumers and growing backlogs. Find documented controls for retention, queue limits, and worker prefetch.
Compare built-in monitoring for Redis Streams and RabbitMQ. Find ways to inspect queue depth, consumer lag, failed deliveries, and worker health in official documentation.
Compare failover behavior for Redis Streams and RabbitMQ quorum queues. Focus on client reconnection, replication requirements, and consequences for running Python workers.
Compare documented backup, restore, and rolling-upgrade procedures for Redis and RabbitMQ when used as task brokers. Identify operational constraints relevant to a small engineering team.
Compare documented TLS, authentication, and access-control options for Redis Streams and RabbitMQ. Focus on giving Python workers only the permissions needed to consume and acknowledge tasks.
